title: COP31 climate talks close to final deal, says summit president
summary: The draft omits mention of the fossil fuels that scientists say are driving climate change, an issue that has been at the center of the fractious talks

blocks.text: JUSTICE. A member of Fridays for Future holds a placard at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey, on November 16, 2026.
The draft omits mention of the fossil fuels that scientists say are driving climate change, an issue that has been at the center of the fractious talks

ANTALYA, Turkey – UN climate talks in Turkey approached a final deal on Sunday, November 22, with the announcement of a new package that COP31 presidents Australia and Turkey hope will achieve consensus on how to advance the fight against global warming.
The new draft deal was released two days after the conference in Antalya was scheduled to end.

If approved, it would acknowledge for the first time that global warming is on course to exceed the 1.5-degree Celsius (2.7-degree Fahrenheit) threshold that countries had sought to preserve, while calling for faster development of carbon-removal technologies to eventually reverse the overshoot.

The draft omits mention of the fossil fuels that scientists say are driving climate change, an issue that has been at the center of the fractious talks. Instead, it includes language referring to a previous COP at which governments had agreed to transition away from oil, gas, and coal.
“We believe that we have put forward a text which all the parties can agree upon,” COP31 President Murat Kurum told a plenary session early on Sunday.
He said the conference would reconvene in the morning to approve the deal.
Environmental group 350.org said it was disappointed by the draft’s failure to mention fossil fuels explicitly, as well as its encouragement of carbon-removal technologies.

“Carbon capture is one of the biggest scams of the overshoot era, and our leaders are on the verge of falling for it,” said Sara Shaw, the group’s campaigns and networks director, referring to the practice of trapping carbon dioxide before it reaches the atmosphere.
Shaw said the draft deal opens the door to more fossil fuel development.
Observers to the closed-door talks said Saudi Arabia and other big oil-producer nations had pushed hard in negotiations for keeping fossil fuels out of the text, and carbon removal in.
A representative for the Saudi delegation declined to comment.

The new text followed intensive consultations between Australia, which is leading the talks, Turkey, which is hosting the meeting, and nearly 200 delegations from many of the world’s richest, poorest, largest and smallest nations.
The presidency gave delegations several hours to raise any objections to the deal, with a session scheduled at 0700 GMT to begin approving it.

Australia’s task, supported by Turkey, has been to find a deal that balances the needs of nations most vulnerable to climate change with those whose economies depend on either the production or consumption of fossil fuels.

This year’s COP is the first since the UN’s environmental body confirmed that the rise in global temperature was set to blow past 1.5 degrees, a threshold all countries agreed over a decade ago to try not to exceed, and beyond which extreme weather impacts intensify. – Rappler.com
